forensic_summary.intervention: I executed a 'Shadow Logistics' campaign to bypass the bureaucratic DFM process. I worked directly with the sheet metal vendor (Mass Precision) to implement a secondary flattening operation and engineered a 'relief cut' pattern to neutralize the PEM stress. For the grounding issue, I designed a massive, custom 'umbilical' grounding strap system that physically bonded the two chassis with near-zero impedance, eliminating the digital ground loop hum.
forensic_summary.result: Recovered the Fader Pan yield from 50% to 98% in two weeks. The grounding architecture silenced the hum, allowing D-Command to ship on time and dominate the mid-tier massive, effectively killing the analog console market for post-production.
forensic_summary.trigger: The 'Mid-Market' Paradox. Marketing demanded a $15k console that 'felt like' our $100k flagship (D-Control). To hit this aggressive price point, we had to split the architecture into a Main Unit and a Fader Expansion, creating a 'Split-Chassis' grounding nightmare. Simultaneously, the first batch of Fader Pans arrived with a 50% rejection rate due to 'Oil-Canning' warpage from high-density PEM insertion.
